summary.plain: XENON100 was a detector holding about 160 kg of liquid xenon in a tunnel at the Gran Sasso underground laboratory in Italy. It looked for flashes of light from dark matter particles hitting xenon atoms, found none, and for a time set the tightest limits then known.
summary.technical: Dual-phase xenon TPC: 62 kg active target inside a 99 kg LXe veto (161 kg total). Science runs of 11.2, 100.9 and 224.6 live days; the 477-live-day combination (Jan 2010 - Jan 2014, 48 kg yr) set a spin-independent limit with a minimum of 1.1e-45 cm^2 at 50 GeV/c^2. Successor of XENON10, predecessor of XENON1T.

technology.quote: uses liquid xenon (LXe) in a time projection chamber (TPC) to search for Xe nuclear recoils
technology.value: Dual-phase liquid xenon time projection chamber
